name: XK Aprosencephaly Syndrome

diagnosticCriteria.formalCriteriaName: Proposed Diagnostic Criteria for XK Aprosencephaly Syndrome

criteria.description: Complete or near-complete absence of the prosencephalon (forebrain) detected by neuroimaging or autopsy
Pathogenic mutation in the XK gene confirmed by genetic testing
Presence of characteristic craniofacial anomalies including microcephaly and midline facial defects
Severe neurological impairment including seizures and developmental arrest
Family history consistent with X-linked inheritance pattern

diagnosticCriteria.minimumForDiagnosis: Presence of aprosencephaly confirmed by imaging or autopsy, pathogenic XK gene mutation, and characteristic craniofacial dysmorphism
diagnosticCriteria.notes: Diagnosis is primarily clinical supported by genetic confirmation; prenatal diagnosis possible via imaging and genetic testing

laboratory: Normal routine blood tests except possible hypoglycemia
Immunological panel may reveal mild immunodeficiency
imaging: Prenatal ultrasound or MRI showing absence of forebrain structures
Postnatal brain MRI confirming aprosencephaly and associated malformations
genetic: Pathogenic variants in XK gene identified by sequencing
X-linked inheritance pattern confirmed by family studies
other: Autopsy findings confirm absence of prosencephalon

distinguishingFeatures: Partial rather than complete absence of forebrain
Predominantly cognitive impairment without major brain malformations

redFlags: Absence of forebrain structures on prenatal imaging
Severe microcephaly with midline facial defects
Family history suggestive of X-linked inheritance
references: Orphanet Report Series: XK Aprosencephaly Syndrome, ORPHA:3469
Genetics Home Reference: XK gene and associated disorders
Recent review on congenital brain malformations and genetic causes, 2025
